why.text: Poor, well-drained soils on the Empordà plain give light, fresh wines with good acidity. Old Garnacha is the classic liqueur wine.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also needle and sparkling wines, liqueur wines from Garnacha and Moscatel, and wines from overripe grapes.

soil.text: Poor, light, acid to neutral soils from conglomerates and sandstones, with good drainage.

tastes.text: Reds: violet-red to brick with age; ripe fruit, balsam, spice; smooth, structured, tannic. Whites: pale yellow; fresh, fruity. Rosés: soft pink to cherry; floral, fruity.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: White: pale to gold, floral, fruity. Black: red-violet, red fruit. Sweet, balanced.

styles.name: Garnacha
styles.text: Ripe or raisined fruit; Ámbar from white or red grapes, Rubí from Garnacha Tinta.

styles.name: Moscatel
styles.text: At least 90% overripe Muscat of Alexandria or Muscat Blanc; sweet, fleshy.

styles.name: Uvas sobremaduradas
styles.text: Overripe grapes, 18% natural alcohol; yellow to amber; dried fruit, long.

why.text: This inland zone has large temperature swings between day and night. They shape the alcohol and aromas of the wines.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also needle wines, sparkling wines and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Inland climate with a wide temperature range between day and night.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: Traditional method, second fermentation in bottle, nine months from tirage to disgorging.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Sweet whites in old-gold colour.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Visible carbon dioxide bubbles without foam; perceptible on the palate.

why.text: Altitude and distance from the sea give the wines their acid core. Wild herbs and forest add aromas such as rosemary and thyme.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also needle wines, sparkling wines (a long local tradition) and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Temperature and rainfall differ from neighbouring areas; altitude, distance from the sea and the pre-coastal range give the wines acidity.

tastes.text: Whites: pale; fresh, floral, herbal, sharp fruit. Rosés: powerful, structured, unctuous. Reds: deep colour, very structured and powerful.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: Fresh citrus and floral fruit; dried fruit and bread from lees; fine bubbles.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Higher acidity with carbon dioxide; fresh, broad.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Overripe or noble-rot grapes; dried fruit, raisin, orange peel, honey.

why.text: Well-drained granite soil with marine remains makes the vines root deep. The mild stress helps regulate yield.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also liqueur wines (rancio, mistela), natural sweet wines and traditional-method sparkling.

soil.text: Granite subsoil with marine remains, breaking into small grains at the surface; permeable.

styles.name: Rancio
styles.text: Oxidative liqueur wine from white Garnacha and Macabeo; a year in oak.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: White-grape free-run must, filtered, wine spirit added.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: Traditional method, second fermentation in bottle, nine months before disgorging.

why.text: Trepat, a grape native to Conca de Barberà, gives rosados and reds with their own character.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also liqueur wines, sparkling wines and needle wines.

tastes.text: Whites: pale green-yellow to deep gold; primary aromas; light, fresh when young. Rosés: bright red-violet to onion-skin; floral, fruity. Reds: intense cherry to ruby; fruity when young, vanilla and toast with barrel ageing.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Amber to opaque; nutty aldehyde notes when aged; warm, unctuous.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: Fresh fruit aromas; fresh, creamy, balanced.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: White or rosé with carbon dioxide; fruity, floral, fresh, slight tickle.

why.text: Soil and climate bring white grapes to ripeness here. The whites get freshness and fruit.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also sparkling, needle and liqueur wines, and sweet wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: A wide temperature gap between day and night in July and August helps red grapes ripen.

tastes.text: Whites: pale to dark yellow; white and tropical fruit, ripe fruit if oaked. Rosés: pale pink to cherry; red fruit, slightly acid, soft, fresh. Reds: garnet when young, tawny when aged.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: Traditional method; at least twelve months from tirage to disgorging.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Second fermentation; carbon dioxide pressure between 1 and 2.5 bar.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Spirit added to must of at least 240 g/l sugar; candied fruit.

styles.name: Dulce de uvas sobremaduradas
styles.text: Made from overripe grapes, no artificial boost to strength.

why.text: Steep slopes have shallow slate soils with bedrock near the surface. The wines are high in dry extract and deep red in colour.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, including single-estate (pago) wines; liqueur wines such as rancio, mistela and natural sweet.

climate.text: Mild and dry; the mountains cut off sea influence and shelter the zone from cold north winds; northwest winds blow.

soil.text: Very steep, shallow soils from slate, low in organic matter, with bedrock close to the surface.

tastes.text: Reds: fruity, floral or mineral aromas; balanced, structured, fresh; oak-aged ones show primary, secondary and tertiary aromas. Whites: fruity, floral or milky; fresh, soft. Rosés: fruity, floral.

why.text: Camp de Tarragona, under direct sea influence, gives Mediterranean wines. Continental Ribera d'Ebre gives fuller reds from Cariñena and Garnacha.

styles.text: Light whites, rosados and reds; also sparkling, needle and liqueur wines such as mistela, moscatel and rancio.

climate.text: Direct sea influence in Camp de Tarragona; a continental influence in Ribera d'Ebre.

tastes.text: Clear, light, balanced wines. Sparkling: fresh, fruity, creamy. Liqueur wines: golden or glossy black, silky, warm, unctuous. Rancio: amber, toasted nuts, spice, dry.

styles.name: Rancio
styles.text: Amber with copper glints; toasted nuts, spice; dry, intense.

styles.name: Mistela, Vimblanc, Moscatel
styles.text: Golden for white grapes, glossy black for red; silky, warm, unctuous.

why.text: Mountains shelter the vines from the sea, giving hot days and cool nights. Old Garnacha and Cariñena vines give full-bodied wines.

styles.text: Mainly reds, with whites and rosados; traditional liqueur wines and natural sweet wines.

climate.text: Mediterranean with some continentality: cold winters, hot dry summers, 500 to 600 mm of rain, mostly spring and autumn; strong day-night contrast.

soil.text: Three kinds: calcareous sedimentary soils, granitic sands (Falset) and slate «llicorella» that adds minerality.

tastes.text: Reds: cherry to tile and amber with age; very ripe fruit, balsamic; broad, round, ripe, velvety tannin. Whites: lemon to straw; ripe fruit, honey; silky. Rosés: bright; cherry, strawberry.

styles.name: Rancio
styles.text: Oxidative ageing in wood or sun-and-night; spice, nuts, toast; dry, full.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: White: honey colour, citrus touch. Black: orange, nuts, lemon. Sweet.

styles.name: Garnacha
styles.text: Overripe grapes, fortified, aged in oak; orange; marmalade, quince; sweet, fresh.

styles.name: Vimblanc
styles.text: From overripe Pansal grape; clean, intense; complex, good finish.

why.text: Calcareous soils give the wines a salty note and a long finish. Garnacha Blanca has a long tradition here.

styles.text: Whites (including single-variety Garnacha Blanca), rosados and reds; also sparkling, needle and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Mediterranean and southern in character, with harvests rich in sugar.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow with grey to gold hints; complex, rich aromas; salty on the palate.

styles.name: Rancio
styles.text: Oxidative ageing in sun and night; at least a year in oak.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: Spirit added to must, mostly Garnacha or Moscatel.

styles.name: Garnacha
styles.text: Liqueur wine from overripe grapes.
